note: lab run PUBLISHES into the tracked book/src/laboratory/generated/STUDY-NAME/ tree even for a throwaway ad-hoc study. Run a one-off measurement study from /tmp and you still get an untracked directory created under a drift-checked path, carrying rows.csv, schema.json, a summary and SVGs. This is worse than ordinary litter because of a hazard CLAUDE.md already names: git diff --exit-code is silently VACUOUS against a path with no index entry, so the only drift check that exists cannot see a stray study directory at all. It caught two of us in one session. An implementer noticed and deleted its own before it could be staged. I did NOT notice mine: an early diagnostic study named probe2 left book/src/laboratory/generated/probe2/ untracked in the MAIN checkout, where it sat unnoticed through the entire campaign until an unrelated directory count came out one short and I went looking. Practice: after ANY ad-hoc lab run, run git status --porcelain book/src/laboratory/generated/ and sweep what you made. Do not trust the drift check to tell you. Unrelated but worth knowing while you are in there: census-of-lands/ under that same tree is GITIGNORED and pre-existing, so it shows as double-bang in git status --ignored and is not a stray.
